title: Independence Day of Ukraine
summary: Independence Day of Ukraine, celebrated on 24 August, is a significant state holiday commemorating the Declaration of Independence in 1991. This day reflects Ukraine's historical journey towards sovereignty and has evolved in public perception and celebration over the years.

sections.heading: Historical Background
paragraphs: Independence Day of Ukraine, known in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] as День Незалежності України (Den Nezalezhnosti Ukrainy), is celebrated on 24 August to mark the Declaration of Independence issued in 1991. Prior to this, the [[ukrainian-diaspora|Ukrainian diaspora]] recognized 22 January, the date of the Declaration of Independence of the [[ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]] in 1918, as the day of independence.

The holiday was first celebrated in its current form on 16 July 1991, coinciding with the first anniversary of the Declaration of State Sovereignty of [[ukraine|Ukraine]], adopted by the [[verkhovna-rada|Verkhovna Rada]] in 1990. Following the Declaration of Independence on 24 August 1991, confirmed by a nationwide referendum on 1 December 1991, the official date of the holiday was changed to 24 August by a parliamentary decision in 1992.

sections.heading: Public Opinion and Popularity
paragraphs: The perception of Independence Day has shifted significantly over the years. In a 2013 poll by the Razumkov Centre, 61% of respondents viewed it as a holiday, while 30.4% considered it an ordinary day off. By 2021, a survey by the [[kyiv|Kyiv]] International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) indicated that 37% of [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]] regarded Independence Day as one of their favorite holidays.

The Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]], which began on 24 February 2022, prompted a reevaluation of the holiday's significance. A March 2024 study by KIIS revealed that the popularity of Independence Day had risen to 64%, reflecting a growing sense of national unity and resilience.

sections.heading: Celebrations and Traditions
paragraphs: Independence Day is typically marked by various celebrations, including military parades in Kyiv, although such parades have been affected by ongoing conflicts. In 2021, a large military parade was held to commemorate the 30th anniversary of independence, featuring over 5,000 troops and numerous foreign military units.

In 2022, celebrations were constrained due to martial law, with public gatherings prohibited. Instead, destroyed Russian military vehicles were displayed in Kyiv, symbolizing resistance against the invasion. The day also saw international support for Ukraine, with events held in various countries to honor its independence.

sections.heading: Significant Events
paragraphs: Notable events in the history of Independence Day include the Chayka Aviation Parade in 1997, which showcased the Ukrainian Air Force, and the postponement of the 2006 celebrations due to a tragic aviation accident that resulted in 170 fatalities.

In 2016, the 'March of the Unconquered' was held following the military parade, honoring those who fought in the Russo-Ukrainian War and the [[euromaidan|Euromaidan]] uprising. The celebrations continue to evolve, reflecting the ongoing struggle for sovereignty and national identity.
